items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "kinetic energy"?
options: A membrane that allows some molecules to pass through but not others.
The surface area of an object divided by its volume.
The net movement of particles from a region of their higher concentration to a region of their lower concentration, down a concentration gradient, as a result of their random movement.
The energy of movement of particles, which drives diffusion.
items.answer: The energy of movement of particles, which drives diffusion.
items.markingKey: Kinetic energy: the energy of movement of particles, which drives diffusion.

items.stem: Explain why diffusion is faster at higher temperatures.
items.answer: Particles have more kinetic energy, so they move faster and spread down the concentration gradient more quickly.
items.markingKey: more kinetic energy [1]; faster random movement [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why small organisms can rely on diffusion across their surface, but large organisms need transport systems.
items.answer: Small organisms have a large surface area to volume ratio and short diffusion distances; in large organisms the ratio is small and cells are far from the surface, so diffusion would be too slow.
items.markingKey: SA:V ratio [1]; distance [1]; diffusion too slow in large organisms [1] [3]

items.stem: Tariq cuts agar cubes containing an indicator, with sides of 4 cm and 5 cm. Calculate the surface area to volume ratio of each cube.
items.answer: 4 cm cube: SA 96 cm², V 64 cm³, ratio 1.5 : 1; 5 cm cube: SA 150 cm², V 125 cm³, ratio 1.2 : 1

items.stem: Priya cuts agar cubes containing an indicator, with sides of 2 cm and 3 cm. Calculate the surface area to volume ratio of each cube and predict which cube will change colour completely first when placed in acid. Explain your prediction.
items.answer: 2 cm cube: SA 24 cm², V 8 cm³, ratio 3 : 1; 3 cm cube: SA 54 cm², V 27 cm³, ratio 2 : 1. The 2 cm cube changes colour first: largest ratio and shortest distance to the centre.
items.markingKey: 24 ÷ 8 = 3 : 1; 54 ÷ 27 = 2 : 1 (SA = 6a², V = a³); smallest cube first [1]; largest SA:V / shortest distance to centre [1] [5]

items.stem: Hana cuts agar cubes containing an indicator, with sides of 0.5 cm, 2 cm and 5 cm. Calculate the surface area to volume ratio of each cube and predict which cube will change colour completely first when placed in acid. Explain your prediction.
items.answer: 0.5 cm cube: SA 1.5 cm², V 0.125 cm³, ratio 12 : 1; 2 cm cube: SA 24 cm², V 8 cm³, ratio 3 : 1; 5 cm cube: SA 150 cm², V 125 cm³, ratio 1.2 : 1. The 0.5 cm cube changes colour first: largest ratio and shortest distance to the centre.
items.markingKey: 1.5 ÷ 0.125 = 12 : 1; 24 ÷ 8 = 3 : 1; 150 ÷ 125 = 1.2 : 1 (SA = 6a², V = a³); smallest cube first [1]; largest SA:V / shortest distance to centre [1] [6]

items.stem: Hana placed cubes of agar containing alkali and phenolphthalein (pink) into dilute hydrochloric acid and timed how long each cube took to become colourless. Results table. Length of side of cube / mm: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. Time to become colourless / s, trial 1: 46, 122, 240, 419, 651; trial 2: 47, 116, 246, 429, 652; trial 3: 45, 122, 351, 434, 665. (a) Identify the anomalous result in the table and state what should be done with it. (b) Calculate the rate of diffusion into the 4 mm cube as mm per second, using half the side length as the distance travelled.
items.answer: (a) Trial 3 at 12 mm (351 s); it should be ignored when calculating the mean (or repeated). (b) 0.043 mm/s
items.markingKey: (a) trial 3 at 12 mm identified [1]; ignore / repeat it [1] [2] (b) distance = 2 mm [1]; ÷ 46 s = 0.043 mm/s [1] [2]

(a) State two variables that should be kept constant in this investigation. (b) Suggest one way to improve this investigation. items.stem: Which term matches this description: "the net movement of particles from a region of their higher concentration to a region of their lower concentration, down a concentration gradient, as a result of their random movement"?
items.answer: Diffusion
items.markingKey: Diffusion: the net movement of particles from a region of their higher concentration to a region of their lower concentration, down a concentration gradient, as a result of their random movement.

items.stem: Which change would increase the rate of diffusion of oxygen into a cell?
items.answer: Increasing the concentration gradient
items.markingKey: Steeper gradient, higher temperature, larger surface area and shorter distance all increase rate.

items.stem: Explain why the walls of alveoli and capillaries are only one cell thick.
items.answer: This gives a short diffusion distance so gases diffuse quickly between air and blood.
items.markingKey: short distance [1]; faster diffusion [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the concentration gradient of oxygen between alveoli and blood is maintained.
items.answer: Ventilation brings fresh air with high oxygen; blood flow carries oxygenated blood away and brings deoxygenated blood, keeping a steep gradient.
items.markingKey: ventilation [1]; blood flow [1] [2]

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "osmosis"?
options: The net movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential (dilute solution) to a region of lower water potential (concentrated solution), through a partially permeable membrane.
Describes a plant cell that is swollen and firm because water has entered and pushes the cytoplasm against the cell wall.
A measure of the tendency of water to move; it is highest in pure water and lower in more concentrated solutions.
The shrinking of the cytoplasm away from the cell wall when a plant cell loses water by osmosis.
items.answer: The net movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential (dilute solution) to a region of lower water potential (concentrated solution), through a partially permeable membrane.
items.markingKey: Osmosis: the net movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential (dilute solution) to a region of lower water potential (concentrated solution), through a partially permeable membrane.

items.stem: Explain why a wilted plant recovers when it is watered.
items.answer: Water enters cells by osmosis from the soil water (higher water potential); cells become turgid and press on each other, supporting the leaves and stems.
items.markingKey: water enters by osmosis [1]; cells turgid [1]; support [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain why plant cells do not burst when placed in pure water.
items.answer: Water enters by osmosis and the cell swells, but the strong cellulose cell wall resists further expansion so the cell becomes turgid, not burst.
items.markingKey: water enters [1]; cell wall resists [1] [2]

items.stem: A potato cylinder had a mass of 2.11 g. After 30 minutes in 0.2 mol/dm³ sucrose solution its mass was 2.19 g. Calculate the percentage change in mass.

Mass before → after: 0 mol/dm³: 2.56 g → 2.86 g; 0.4 mol/dm³: 2.18 g → 2.13 g; 0.8 mol/dm³: 2.51 g → 2.19 g; 1 mol/dm³: 2.23 g → 1.85 g. (a) Calculate the percentage change in mass for each concentration. (b) State which concentration caused the largest loss in mass.
items.markingKey: (a) 11.7%; -2.3%; -12.7%; -17% (all correct with signs) [2] (b) 1 mol/dm³ [1] [3]

(a) Calculate the percentage change in mass for each concentration. (b) Estimate the concentration of sucrose that would cause no change in mass. (c) Explain the change in mass at the highest concentration.
items.answer: (a) 0: 9.1%; 0.2: 1.7%; 0.4: -4%; 0.6: -10%; 0.8: -13.3%; 1: -17.3% (b) about 0.26 mol/dm³ (c) The solution has a lower water potential than the cells, so water leaves the cells by osmosis; mass decreases.

items.stem: A red blood cell is placed in distilled water. What happens?
items.answer: It swells and bursts
items.markingKey: Water enters by osmosis (higher water potential outside); with no cell wall the membrane bursts.

items.stem: A plant cell is placed in a concentrated sugar solution. What is it likely to become?
items.answer: Plasmolysed
items.markingKey: Water leaves by osmosis, the vacuole and cytoplasm shrink and pull away from the wall.

items.stem: Explain why doctors use a drip with a salt concentration equal to that of blood plasma, not pure water.
items.answer: Pure water has a higher water potential than cells, so water would enter red blood cells by osmosis and they would burst (lysis); an isotonic solution causes no net movement.
items.markingKey: osmosis into cells [1]; lysis [1]; equal concentrations = no net movement [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain why putting salt on a slug kills it.
items.answer: The salt solution on its moist skin has a lower water potential, so water leaves the slug cells by osmosis and it becomes dehydrated.
items.markingKey: lower water potential outside [1]; water lost by osmosis [1] [2]

items.stem: Which term is defined as "the process in cells that releases the energy needed for active transport"?
items.answer: Respiration
items.markingKey: Respiration: the process in cells that releases the energy needed for active transport.

items.stem: Root hair cells contain many mitochondria. Explain why.
items.answer: They absorb mineral ions by active transport, which needs energy released by aerobic respiration in mitochondria.
items.markingKey: active transport of ions [1]; energy from respiration in mitochondria [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why waterlogged soils can reduce the uptake of mineral ions by plants.
items.answer: Waterlogged soil has little oxygen, so root cells cannot respire aerobically and release less energy for active transport of ions.
items.markingKey: little oxygen [1]; less respiration / energy [1]; less active transport [1] [3]

items.stem: The concentration of magnesium ions in soil water is 0.37 mmol/dm³ and in the root hair cells of a plant is 7.4 mmol/dm³. (a) Calculate how many times more concentrated the ions are inside the cells. (b) Name the process by which the ions are absorbed and explain your answer.
items.answer: (a) 20 times (b) Active transport: the ions move against a concentration gradient, which needs energy from respiration.
items.markingKey: (a) 7.4 ÷ 0.37 = 20 [1] (b) active transport [1]; against concentration gradient using energy [1] [3]

items.stem: The concentration of magnesium ions in soil water is 0.05 mmol/dm³ and in the root hair cells of a plant is 2 mmol/dm³. (a) Calculate how many times more concentrated the ions are inside the cells. (b) Name the process by which the ions are absorbed and explain your answer. (c) Predict and explain the effect on ion uptake if the soil is waterlogged.
items.answer: (a) 40 times (b) Active transport: the ions move against a concentration gradient, which needs energy from respiration. (c) Uptake decreases: little oxygen for aerobic respiration, so less energy for active transport.
items.markingKey: (a) 2 ÷ 0.05 = 40 [1] (b) active transport [1]; against concentration gradient using energy [1] (c) uptake falls [1]; less oxygen → less respiration → less energy [1] [5]

items.stem: Explain how protein carriers in the membrane are involved in active transport.
items.answer: A carrier protein binds a specific molecule or ion on one side of the membrane, changes shape using energy from respiration and releases it on the other side.
items.markingKey: binds specific substance [1]; shape change using energy / release on other side [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the concentration of glucose in the blood leaving the small intestine can be higher than in the gut contents after a meal is nearly absorbed.
items.answer: Glucose continues to be absorbed by active transport into the villi cells against the concentration gradient, so it is absorbed even when the gut has less glucose than the blood.
items.markingKey: against gradient [1]; active transport uses energy [1] [2]

items.stem: Tomás says: "Active transport gets its energy from sunlight." Explain whether Tomás is correct.
items.answer: The energy for active transport comes from respiration in the cell.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: The energy for active transport comes from respiration in the cell. [2]

items.stem: What provides the energy for diffusion?
options: Energy from respiration in the cell
The kinetic energy of the random movement of particles
items.answer: The kinetic energy of the random movement of particles
items.markingKey: Diffusion is passive: it uses no energy from respiration.

items.stem: Explain why diffusion is described as a passive process.
items.answer: It does not need energy from respiration; it relies on the random kinetic energy of particles moving down a concentration gradient.
items.markingKey: no energy from respiration [1]; random movement down gradient [1] [2]

items.stem: A drop of food dye in still water spreads out slowly even though no one stirs it. Explain why.
items.answer: The dye and water particles move randomly; there is a net movement of dye particles from where they are concentrated to where they are less concentrated until evenly spread.
items.markingKey: random movement [1]; net movement high → low concentration [1] [2]

items.stem: State the direction in which urea diffuses between the liver cell and the blood plasma, and explain why.
items.answer: From the liver cell to the blood plasma, because it is produced by deamination in the liver, so there is a concentration gradient.
items.markingKey: direction liver cell → blood plasma [1]; higher concentration in liver cell / gradient explained [1] [2]

items.stem: Describe and explain how surface area, temperature, concentration gradient and distance affect the rate of diffusion.
items.answer: Larger surface area: more particles cross at once, faster. Higher temperature: more kinetic energy, faster. Steeper gradient: greater net movement, faster. Shorter distance: particles reach destination sooner, faster.
items.markingKey: each factor with correct direction and explanation [4]; example from living organisms [1] [5]

items.stem: Which statement about osmosis is correct?
options: Water moves from a concentrated solution to a dilute solution
Solute molecules move through the membrane from concentrated to dilute
Water moves from a dilute solution to a concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane
Water moves only when energy from respiration is used
items.answer: Water moves from a dilute solution to a concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane
items.markingKey: Water moves down its water potential gradient (high to low water potential).

items.stem: Visking tubing containing sugar solution is placed in water. Explain why the liquid rises up a capillary tube attached to the tubing.
items.answer: Water moves into the tubing by osmosis (from higher to lower water potential) through the partially permeable membrane; sugar molecules are too large to leave; the volume inside increases.
items.markingKey: osmosis into tubing [1]; sugar cannot pass out [1]; volume increases [1] [3]

items.stem: Tariq places red blood cells in one dish and onion epidermis cells in another, both in a 0.9% salt solution (same as blood plasma), and observes them after 20 minutes. (a) Explain these observations. (b) Suggest why a student should view the cells at the same magnification before and after. (c) Explain why turgor pressure is important for a non-woody plant.
items.answer: (a) Water potentials are equal, so there is no net movement of water by osmosis. (b) So that changes in size can be compared fairly. (c) Turgid cells press against each other, supporting stems and leaves so that leaves are held up to the light; loss of turgor causes wilting.
